corpusSummary: The corpus assembles 2026 social-science papers on large language models across health, education, policy, climate, and media, emphasizing human–AI interaction, LLM-powered research workflows, and governance. It reveals varied trust and perceived humanness, safety and fairness concerns, and the dual role of LLMs as analytic tools and educational aids. Reliability gaps and misinformation risks call for human oversight and transparent, ethically guided adoption.

themes.name: Trust and social dynamics of AI use
themes.description: Trust, perceived humanness, disclosure, and the social dynamics of AI adoption across consumer, educational, clinical, and organizational contexts.

themes.name: LLMs as research tools and agents in social science
themes.description: LLMs are used as methodological collaborators, agents in simulations, and analytic aids—transforming framing, coding, data extraction, policy analysis, and governance, while highlighting validation and ethical concerns.

themes.name: AI in education and learning
themes.description: GenAI influences teaching, learning, and design education, shaping pedagogy, literacy development, and student experiences, with benefits and risks like overreliance and ethics.

themes.name: Safety, fairness, and governance of AI
themes.description: Across domains, researchers evaluate safety, equity, bias, ethics, misinformation, and governance frameworks guiding responsible AI deployment.
